widget.cell.centriole.fact: Found in animal cells; most plant cells don't have them.
widget.cell.centriole.fn: Help organise the spindle fibres that pull chromosomes apart when the cell divides.
widget.cell.centriole.name: Centrioles
widget.cell.chloroplast.fn: Contains green chlorophyll that traps sunlight to make food (glucose) by photosynthesis.
widget.cell.chloroplast.name: Chloroplast
widget.cell.cytoplasm.fn: The jelly-like fluid that fills the cell. Most chemical reactions happen here.
widget.cell.cytoplasm.name: Cytoplasm
widget.cell.er.fact: Rough ER is studded with ribosomes, which makes it look bumpy.
widget.cell.er.fn: A network of folded membranes that transports materials. Rough ER (with ribosomes) makes proteins; smooth ER makes lipids.
widget.cell.er.name: Endoplasmic reticulum
widget.cell.golgi.fact: It looks like a stack of flattened pancakes.
widget.cell.golgi.fn: The packaging and shipping centre: it modifies proteins and packs them into vesicles to send around or out of the cell.
widget.cell.golgi.name: Golgi apparatus
widget.cell.hint: Tap a part of the cell to learn what it does.
widget.cell.lysosome.fact: Often called the cell's recycling centre.
widget.cell.lysosome.fn: Contains digestive enzymes that break down worn-out parts, food particles and invading germs.
widget.cell.lysosome.name: Lysosome
widget.cell.membrane.fact: It's 'selectively permeable' — like a bouncer letting only some molecules through.
widget.cell.membrane.fn: A thin, flexible layer that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
widget.cell.membrane.name: Cell membrane
widget.cell.mitochondria.fact: Mitochondria have their own DNA, inherited from your mother.
widget.cell.mitochondria.fn: The powerhouse: it releases energy from glucose by aerobic respiration, making ATP.
widget.cell.mitochondria.name: Mitochondria
widget.cell.nucleus.fact: The dark spot inside is the nucleolus, which makes ribosomes.
widget.cell.nucleus.fn: The control centre. It holds DNA — the instructions for building and running the cell.
widget.cell.nucleus.name: Nucleus
widget.cell.ribosome.fact: A single cell can have millions of ribosomes.
widget.cell.ribosome.fn: Tiny factories that build proteins by reading instructions copied from DNA (mRNA).
widget.cell.ribosome.name: Ribosomes
widget.cell.vacuole.fact: A plant's central vacuole can fill up to 90% of the cell!
widget.cell.vacuole.fn: A storage sac for water, sugars and waste. In plants one large central vacuole keeps the cell firm (turgid).
widget.cell.vacuole.name: Vacuole
widget.cell.wall.fact: Only plants, fungi and bacteria have cell walls — animal cells don't.
widget.cell.wall.fn: A rigid layer made of cellulose outside the membrane. It gives the plant cell shape and support.
widget.cell.wall.name: Cell wall
